profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer Technical Lead at Google
profile.summary:
Solving difficult UI problems in the Key and Secret Management space of Google Cloud Console. Chris works as a feature lead for a suite of Google Cloud's cybersecurity products, where he designs, implements and launches features to protect corporate data under international privacy regulations from cyberattacks. With 15+ launches globally, initiatives he has led have been featured in publications such as Forbes, TechCrunch, and Fortune Magazine.

Chris is a Yale graduate with a B.S in Computer Science and Electrical Engineering with a lifelong background in digital media design. Work primarily in mobile application, full-stack, or web development. Former developer of a mobile app called MovesU which used GPS to tell Yalies how many people are at parties on campus in real-time. The app has been rewritten in React Native, Angular, and TypeScript. Chris has worked independently on a music app that uses Google's Flutter framework and Spotify’s API. Chris enjoys researching and staying up-to-date with the latest frontend technologies and also continues to hone graphic, motion, music and video production, and game design/networking skills.

GitHub: https://github.com/mooreorless555

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
Frontend UI and full-stack work on Google Cloud Console:
  - Cloud Shell
  - Cloud Workstations

Feature lead for several projects each involving:
  - Authoring of peer-reviewed proposal and technical design documents
  - Project scoping and task breakdowns
  - Cross-team collaboration with Product, UI/UX teams and integrating/core teams across the relevant stacks.
  - General technical implementation of the feature
  - Regular meetings/syncs with relevant stakeholders
  - Maintaining feature documentation and playbooks
  - Integration testing (end-to-end and hermetic)
  - Implementation of metrics and analytics based on aligned customer user journeys.
  - Organizing "bug hunts" with team and stakeholders to test the feature and resolve outstanding issues before launch
  - Launching feature and closely monitoring traffic during ramp-up

  - Security Command Center
  - Key Management Service
  - Secret Manager
  - Binary Authorization

positions.title: Founder, App Developer
positions.description:
Mobile party app for Yale students that uses GPS to figure out how many people are at parties on campus in real-time. Integrated with Google Maps, SendGrid and Facebook APIs. Used shallow database nesting to greatly increase query speed of friends and emails in the NoSQL database. Implemented caching and lazy loading for large lists of Facebook friends. Redeveloped MovesU in React Native, Angular/Node.js, and TypeScript. One of 2 students to selected to speak at TEDxYale entrepreneuership workshop. App received mentions in the Yale Daily News. At its peak, the app was used by 20% of Yale undergraduates (Listed as MovesU in the Google Play and iOS App stores).

Website and app store links: movesapp.com (EDIT: domain sold to another company)
Yale Daily News mention: https://yaledailynews.com/blog/2017/09/12/new-party-app-moves-makes-its-move/

positions.title: iOS Developer Intern
positions.description: Designed and developed a large feature for production in the Grubhub iOS 12 app involving Siri's machine learning framework to predict when diners want to reorder their favorite meals and prompt a reorder via push notification. Implemented polymorphic protocols and methods to ensure feature scalability. Worked with product and design teams directly to create new UI/UX elements. Gained substantial experience with agile development and kanban. Implemented unit and UI automation tests as well as fixed longstanding user interface bugs.
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · Teamwork · Front-End Development

positions.title: Lead Instructor
positions.description: Taught courses in C++, Python, Assembly, JavaScript and videogame design to children aged 10-17. Wrote C++ game server which automated camp-wide gaming tournaments and allowed more campers to participate in multiplayer matches simultaneously. Managed camp operations- spoke to and resolved issues with parents. Supervised on weekdays and weekends. Regularly modified curricula on the fly to fit my class’ needs. Earned consistently high ratings from students, camp director, and hiring manager.

positions.title: Game Design Instructor
positions.description: Taught 8 seminars in game design using Unreal Engine 4, Torchlight II, Valve Hammer Editor and Photoshop 5 days a week to teens ages 13 – 17. Supervised on weekdays and weekends. Created and moderated camp-wide gaming server. Regularly modified curricula on the fly to fit my class’ needs. Earned consistently high ratings from students, camp director, and hiring manager.

positions.title: Yale Freshman Class Council Marketing Chair
positions.description: Filmed and edited promotional videos for classwide events such as the Freshman Barbeque and Freshman Dance. Programmed the event webpage for the annual Harvard vs. Yale football game. Designed backdrop photos for the Freshman Dance as well as team shirts for the Freshman Olympics.

positions.title: Volunteer Counselor
positions.description: Supervised and participated in daily activities with the children. Spent final week creating an upbeat video montage of the campers and counselors which the club now uses as a promotional advertisement.

company.name: Boys & Girls Club of New Rochelle

positions.title: General Counselor
positions.description: Supervised a group of children each day, escorted them to all of their sports, swim and art activities and participated in such. Voted Counselor-of-the-Week one week.

honors.title: Piertotum Locomotor, Goblet of Mods Contest Gameplay Grand Winner
honors.description:
The Goblet of Mods was a 6-weeklong game modding hackathon for "Hogwarts Legacy", the popular Harry Potter adventure game with a grand prize pool of $125,000 sponsored by Warner Bros. and Curseforge.

Using the modding toolkit, which was a modified version of Unreal Engine 4, I recreated the iconic summoning spell Piertotum Locomotor that allows players to summon Hogwarts' armored statues to defend them in battle. The project involved creating custom animations, cutscenes and game logic. The project was awarded $500 in the Weekly Winners category and $2500 as a grand prize winner in the Gameplay category for a total of $3000.
honors.issuer: Issued by Warner Bros. x Curseforge · Mar 2025

honors.title: JumpMS, MapleJam 2024 Game Development Hackathon Winner
honors.description: MapleJam ‘24 was a month-long hackathon to develop a game using Nexon's new MapleStory Worlds platform (similar to Roblox) using the LUA programming language. JumpMS (my project) won the Multiplayer category and was awarded $2000.

projects.title: MXFY for Spotify
projects.description:
MXFY for Spotify is a Flutter web app that lets you tell Spotify when to start and stop songs in your playlists. You can then add transition and impact sound effects to create a mix that sounds like it's coming from a real DJ.

Link: https://mxfyapp.surge.sh/#/
